result.markdown: --- subtitle: "Arithmetic intensity, the memory hierarchy, and honest performance claims" description: "Why an operation count cannot identify the resource that sets elapsed time." number-offset: 0 jupyter: python3 phenomenon_id: c01-count-not-cost claim_ids: [c01-roofline-001] threads: {} lenses: geometric: quiet dynamic: supporting algorithmic: primary --- # The Count Is Not the Cost {#c01} Geometric quiet · Dynamic supporting · Algorithmic primary Consider two computations on $N$ stored FP32 values. A copy performs no floating-point arithmetic and moves at least $8N$ bytes: one read and one write. A fused affine transform $y_i=ax_i+b$ performs $2N$ floating-point operations and has the same dominant traffic when $a$ and $b$ remain in a fast store. Their operation counts differ infinitely as a ratio; their bandwidth ceilings are essentially the same. Now compare a square matrix product of order $n=512$. The conventional count is $2n^3$ operations. Its compulsory traffic under an idealized one-read, one-write model is $12n^2$ bytes, so its arithmetic intensity is $n/6=85.33$ operations per byte. The affine transform has intensity $2/8=0.25$. On a hypothetical machine whose peak arithmetic-to-bandwidth ratio is 20, one falls below the balance point and the other lies above it. The larger operation count can be the computation with more opportunity to reuse data. ::: {.callout-important title="Prediction"} If a proposed method removes half the multiplications but doubles compulsory traffic, which change should improve elapsed time? The counts alone cannot answer. Name the machine balance and the achieved data reuse first. ::: ## Two resource clocks {#sec-c01-two-clocks} Let $F$ be the required operations, $Q$ the bytes transferred through a declared boundary, $P_{\max}$ peak arithmetic rate, and $B$ peak bandwidth. The two unavoidable time lower bounds are $$ T\geq \frac{F}{P_{\max}},\qquad T\geq\frac{Q}{B}. $$ {#eq-c01-resource-times} With arithmetic intensity $I=F/Q$, achieved performance $P=F/T$ obeys the following deliberately small theorem. ::: {#thm-c01-roofline phenomenon_id="c01-count-not-cost"} ### Two-resource performance ceiling Under the declared operation count, traffic boundary, peak arithmetic rate, and peak bandwidth, $$ P\leq \min(P_{\max},BI). $$ {#eq-c01-roofline} ::: ### Proof Invert each inequality in @eq-c01-resource-times and multiply by $F$. The arithmetic bound gives $P\leq P_{\max}$; the traffic bound gives $P\leq BF/Q=BI$. Both must hold. The bend occurs at the **machine balance** $I_*=P_{\max}/B$. This diagram is the roofline model [@williams2009]. It is an upper envelope, not a prediction that a kernel reaches either roof. :::: {.plan-code} ::: {.plan} 1. Read the committed C01 model calculation. 2. Declare one hypothetical machine balance. 3. Plot the bandwidth and arithmetic ceilings. 4. Place the vector transform and matrix product on the same axes. 5. Check the registered arithmetic intensities before interpretation. ::: ::: {#cell-fig-c01-roofline .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-summary="Code: place two exact traffic models on a declared roofline"} import json from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np # [1] claim = json.loads(Path("artifacts/claims/c01-roofline-001.json").read_text()) # [2] balance = claim["result"]["machine_balance_flop_per_byte"] # [3] intensity = np.logspace(-2, 3, 300) ceiling = np.minimum(intensity / balance, 1.0) fig, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.8)) axis.loglog(intensity, ceiling, color="#5b4b8a", linewidth=2) # [4] points = { "fused affine": claim["result"]["vector_affine_intensity"], "512×512 product": claim["result"]["gemm_intensity"], } for label, value in points.items(): axis.scatter(value, min(value / balance, 1.0), s=55) axis.annotate( label, (value, min(value / balance, 1.0)), xytext=(5, 8), textcoords="offset points", ) axis.set( xlabel="arithmetic intensity (operation/byte)", ylabel="fraction of arithmetic peak", ) axis.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25) fig.tight_layout() # [5] assert np.isclose(points["fused affine"], 0.25) assert np.isclose(points["512×512 product"], 512 / 6) print("claim c01-roofline-001: verified") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` claim c01-roofline-001: verified ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![One operation count is not one cost. Under the declared two-resource model, the vector transform lies below the balance point while the reused matrix product lies above it.](01-count-not-cost_files/figure-html/fig-c01-roofline-output-2.png){#fig-c01-roofline width=681 height=354 fig-alt='Log-log roofline chart with a sloped bandwidth ceiling meeting a flat arithmetic ceiling at intensity 20. The vector transform is at intensity 0.25 on the sloped branch; the order-512 matrix product is at intensity about 85 on the flat branch.'} ::: ::: :::: ## The denominator is an algorithmic choice {#sec-c01-denominator} Traffic has no meaning until its boundary is named. Bytes between registers and a first-level cache, between cache and main memory, and between host and accelerator are different denominators. Tiling changes $Q$ by retaining a working set near arithmetic units. Fusion changes $Q$ by keeping an intermediate value from making a round trip. Recompute can deliberately increase $F$ to reduce $Q$. C11 will return to exactly that trade when it checkpoints derivative state. This also foreshadows the numerical-stability thread that C02 seeds. A fused operation can change both traffic and rounding: eliminating an intermediate store may eliminate one rounding step. A performance transformation is therefore part of the numerical contract, not merely a scheduling detail. ::: {.callout-warning title="Named wrong answer: fewer operations means faster"} Fewer operations is evidence only after the limiting resource is identified. It may improve a compute-limited kernel, do nothing to a bandwidth-limited kernel, or make the kernel slower by destroying reuse or fusion. ::: ## Hardware-claim boundary {#sec-c01-boundary} The roofline is useful because it makes omissions visible. Peak values may be unreachable; compulsory traffic can underestimate actual traffic; latency, launch overhead, synchronization, occupancy, instruction mix, and access regularity remain outside @eq-c01-roofline. CPU simulation of FP16 behavior is not evidence of accelerator timing. Any measured claim later in this book must name the device, software stack, warmup, repetitions, statistic, and traffic boundary—or be labeled a model calculation or pinned artifact. ## Check yourself {#sec-c01-check} A kernel performs $10^{10}$ operations and moves $10^9$ bytes. On a device with $P_{\max}=10^{13}$ operation/s and $B=5\times10^{11}$ byte/s, its intensity is 10 and the machine balance is 20. The model ceiling is therefore $BI=5\times10^{12}$ operation/s, the bandwidth branch. Halving $F$ while leaving $Q$ unchanged also halves intensity; it does not halve the traffic time lower bound. ## Okay, so — {#sec-c01-recap} - **Inherited:** asymptotic operation counts remain indispensable scaling summaries. - **Changed:** elapsed-time reasoning now requires a declared traffic denominator and machine balance. - **Instrumented:** claim `c01-roofline-001` places two exact models on the same ceiling. - **Established:** $P\leq\min(P_{\max},BI)$ follows from two resource lower bounds. - **Unresolved:** real executions move more state through more levels; C02 asks which state an online computation must retain. ## Sources and further reading {#sec-c01-sources} The roofline formulation and its machine-balance interpretation follow @williams2009. The instructor source is the Spring 2026 memory-hierarchy and roofline deck; its hardware slogans were replaced here by an explicit claim boundary and an exact model calculation. ## Exercises {#sec-c01-exercises} 1. **(Pencil.)** Recompute the matrix-product intensity if one input matrix is reread four times. State the traffic boundary. 2. **(Code.)** For three hypothetical machine balances, redraw the figure and report which classifications change. Do not time the plotting code. 3. **(Audit.)** Find one paper that reports a speedup. Separate its operation count, modeled traffic, measured elapsed time, hardware identity, and baseline. Which claim is actually supported?
